title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.22124v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content-safety red-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems. We propose PROBE (Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration), an algorithm for training LLM-based auditors that interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe them for policy vio

translated_title: PROBE：学习审计工具使用型大语言模型智能体的政策合规性
translated_abstract: 现代智能体系统通过外部工具扩展了语言模型的能力，使其能够通过多轮交互完成复杂任务。当这些智能体被部署在具有重大影响的环境中时，它们通常受到关于定价、隐私、确认、安全及其他要求的政策约束。然而，现有的评估方法存在一个关键空白：能力基准衡量的是智能体能完成什么，内容安全红队测试衡量的是有害内容生成，但两者都无法检验智能体在其他方面有效的工具使用过程中是否遵守预定义的政策。这类政策违规难以审计，因为其影响可能只有在若干轮交互后才显现，可能跨越多次工具调用，或出现在下游系统中。我们提出了PROBE（Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration，通过行为探索进行政策规则观察），这是一种训练基于大语言模型的审计员的算法，这些审计员以真实用户的身份与已部署的智能体进行交互，并探测其政策违规行为。
tldr: 提出了PROBE算法，通过训练基于大语言模型的审计员以真实用户身份与已部署的智能体交互，探测并审计那些效果延迟显现、跨越多次工具调用的难以发现的政策违规行为。
en_tdlr: PROBE is an algorithm that trains LLM-based auditors to interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe for hard-to-detect policy violations whose effects may emerge only after multiple turns or tool calls.
